planting.note: Plant container-grown trees in spring in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil with dappled or afternoon shade; site permanently while young since stewartias establish slowly and resent root disturbance.

directions: Bred at the U.S. National Arboretum from Stewartia monadelpha and Stewartia rostrata parentage, 'Skyrocket' is prized for an unusually narrow, tightly upright, columnar habit that sets it apart from every other garden stewartia and makes it useful as a vertical accent in courtyards and other tight side-yard planting strips where a spreading tree would not fit. It still delivers the classic stewartia multi-season package on a narrower frame: small white camellia-like flowers in summer, orange to reddish-purple fall foliage, and smoothly exfoliating bark in mottled gray and cinnamon tones for winter interest. Grow in moist, acidic, well-drained, humus-rich soil with morning sun and afternoon shade, and keep soil evenly moist, since this hybrid shares the genus's intolerance of drought and heavy, poorly drained ground.
